_about: Deliberate differences between deploy/compose/docker-compose.yml and the ECS container definitions (demo-lite/containers.tf) in the environment and secret names of the four app services. tests/task.tftest.hcl (run ecs_names_match_compose) fails on every other difference, in both directions, and on entries here that are no longer true. A name is compared in Spring's relaxed spelling (lower case, no . _ -): SPRING_DATASOURCE_PASSWORD equals the compose secret target spring.datasource.password. 'aliases': one compose name that ECS spells with other names; 'services.<svc>.compose_only' / 'ecs_only': names only one side has.

openai_api_key.why: Compose mounts the key as the configtree file openai_api_key; ECS can only inject env vars, so it uses the relaxed-binding spelling of saiman.router.openai.api-key. RouterPropertiesBinder reads both.

SPRING_DATA_REDIS_URL.why: ECS Redis requires a password. Spring Boot ignores spring.data.redis.password when spring.data.redis.url is set (credentials come from the URL), and the password is a secret that cannot be written into an env var URL, so ECS uses host and port. Compose has no Redis password.

ecs_only.SPRING_DATA_REDIS_PASSWORD: ECS Redis runs with --requirepass (compose Redis has no password); the password is the SSM secret redis_password.
ecs_only.MANAGEMENT_ENDPOINT_HEALTH_SHOW_COMPONEN: Component names and statuses (never details) in /actuator/health, so a failed demo-up shows which component is DOWN (readiness.sh); the services default to show-components: never. Loopback only; nginx does not route /actuator.

compose_only.SAIMAN_AUTH_SERVICE_TOKENS_EVALS_SHA256: The evals harness is not part of the AWS demo, so seller-api has no evals service token to verify.
